_about: Every number the simulation relies on that is NOT measured. Values tagged ASSUMED are placeholders until the site walk / counts replace them; DATA marks values taken from a source. Edit this file, then `python run.py` to rebuild everything.

time._note: Weekday morning peak, 9:30-10:30 am. Both published counts near the loop peak then: 10-11 am between Indiranagar and Domlur (3,869 vehicles against 2,430 at 8-9), 9:30-10:30 on Hosur Road south of Silk Board. Vehicle volumes below were NOT rescaled when the hour moved from 8-9 am; at the Indiranagar-Domlur count point the busier hour carries about 45% more. Warm-up is simulated but excluded from all metrics.

signals._tag: ASSUMED - replace with timings measured at A, B, C on the walk. Junction signals are 'actuated': green time follows the queues (between min and max green), as a stand-in for police-managed junctions. Set junction_type to 'static' for fixed timings.
signals._signalised_note: DATA for A and B (tender route map, page 23: Signal-1 is at junction A, and no signal is drawn at the Madiwala underpass junction B; it is a schematic, so confirm on the walk). The corridor report's 'existing traffic signals' drawing of 23 Jan 2026 agrees: a signal at A, none at B, and the next one on Hosur Road is at Madiwala Road, south of B. ASSUMED for C, which is not on the route map. Junctions not listed here have no signal even where OpenStreetMap maps one.
signals._turn_note: ASSUMED: at signalised junctions the lane next to the median on an approach of 3 or more lanes is a turn-only lane (right turn and U-turn across oncoming traffic), with its own green of protected_turn_green_s. Without it the model lets those turns go only in gaps in oncoming traffic, which never come at these volumes, and the queue blocks the whole approach. Confirm the real lane use and phases on the walk.

network._tag: ASSUMED - corrections to the OpenStreetMap network; confirm on the walk

lane_overrides._note: OSM way id -> vehicle lanes. The two slip roads at junction B carry the Inner Ring Road <-> Hosur Road south turns (about 1,150 veh/h each way per the OD study). OSM gives 1 lane (172853384) or no lane count (684917326); one lane at a signal cannot carry that flow, so 2 lanes are assumed.

entrance_extensions._note: OSM way id -> metres added before its first node. The Hosur Road south entrance was 33 m long, so any queue blocked every vehicle entering there; the extension gives queues room to form inside the model.

foot_over_bridges._note: DATA for position (OpenStreetMap footway bridges and their stairs, osm/footbridges.osm.xml; two span Sarjapura Road on the loop, also shown on the BMRCL survey sheets). ASSUMED: walking speed on stairs, and that each stair foot joins the footpath of the nearest carriageway within connect_within_m.

vehicle_mix._tag: DATA, but not from the loop - classified count between Indiranagar and Domlur, 6 am-8 pm on 25 Apr 2025 (corridor project report section 5.1; the OD & toll analysis reuses it). About 6 km north of the loop. Buses removed; they come from GTFS

od_peak_veh_per_hour._tag: ASSUMED for every movement; nothing has been counted on the loop. IRR>HS and HS>IRR (1,150) borrow the Indiranagar-Domlur count, about 6 km north: 27,300 motor vehicles in 14 hours, of which 2,430 in the 8-9 am hour both ways, halved. The day's split there was 60/40 by direction, and its busiest hour was 10-11 am (3,869), see reference_counts.
od_peak_veh_per_hour._gateways: Gateways: HN Hosur Rd north (beyond C), HS Hosur Rd south (beyond B), SE Sarjapura Rd east (beyond A), IRR Inner Ring Rd / 100 Ft Rd north-east of A, TW Tavarekere Main Rd west of C. Tavarekere Main Rd is one-way westbound in OSM, so TW is an exit only.

reference_counts._about: Published counts near the loop, for reference only; no script reads this block. None was taken on the loop roads.

indiranagar_domlur_2025.source: Corridor project report (dpr-omr-to-silk-board.pdf) section 5.1, table 5-1; 25 Apr 2025, 6 am-8 pm, one working day
indiranagar_domlur_2025.where: 100 Feet Road / Inner Ring Road between Indiranagar and Domlur, about 6 km north of junction A

hosur_road_cordon_2024.source: Tunnel project report (Feb 2025) tables 54-56, cordon point 9, video count, Aug 2024, 24 hours
hosur_road_cordon_2024.where: Labelled 'NH-44 near Madiwala footbridge'; the report's survey map (figure 64) puts it south of Silk Board junction, so it includes Outer Ring Road traffic and is an upper bound for Hosur Road at the loop

madiwala_junction_design_flow.source: Corridor project report section 4.4.5; basis not stated

signals_drawing_2026.source: traffic-signals-under.pdf, 'Project road showing existing traffic signals', 23 Jan 2026, not to scale
signals_drawing_2026.finding: Signal-10 at junction A (Sarjapura Road x Inner Ring Road). No signal at the Madiwala underpass junction B. Signal-11 on Hosur Road at Madiwala Road, south of B and outside the loop. Junction C is off the project road and not covered.

flyover_opened._tag: DATA-derived, not from the loop: OD study expects 12,357-16,842 of the 27,300 vehicles counted in 14 hours between Indiranagar and Domlur (45-62%) to divert to the elevated corridor; midpoint used

buses._tag: DATA for routes and timetabled times (BMTC GTFS by Vonter, ODbL, Monday service); ASSUMED dwell time

pedestrians._tag: ASSUMED - replace with the P1-P6 crossing counts from the walk
pedestrians._step_free_note: ASSUMED: 1 in 10 people walking cannot use stairs (wheelchair users, prams, many older people, people with luggage), so they never use the foot over bridges; they walk at 1.0 m/s. The same people in every scenario. No local figure; a common planning allowance.
pedestrians._red_light_note: NOT MODELLED: people crossing on red when traffic leaves a gap. SUMO's two ways of allowing it (jmDriveAfterRedTime on people; giving crossings a give-way green) were tested on a test junction: both send people into moving traffic, vehicle delay rose from 17 to 91 s and people lost more time, not less. So detours here assume people wait for the green; real detours and waits are shorter.

trial_crossings._tag: Positions from the study's crossing analysis (data/crossings.geojson): distance in metres along each road from its first junction. 100 Ft Rd only within the feasible zone 225-438 m (ramp wall 45-225 m).

proposals._about: Proposals drawn on the website's Draw tab, turned into scenarios by scripts/make_proposal.py. Each scenario is today's network (no metro, tunnel or flyover) plus the drawing. A drawing says where, not how, so each entry records how each kind of mark is read. Same traffic, people and buses as the baseline.

proposal_151126.label: Planner proposal at C
proposal_151126._readings: Agreed 16 Nov 2026: zebras are signalised crossings (fixed plan as the trial crossings); Zone 1 islands closed to traffic; Zone 2 widened footpath (a guess); Zone 3 is the bus stop. ASSUMED by us: each Zone 3 shape takes over the nearest existing bus stop in the same direction; a shape of 200 m2 or more is an off-road bay where a stopped bus leaves the running lane; the two new roads are one-lane links at 20 km/h for all vehicles, each joining the road nearest its drawn ends and running in the direction traffic can flow - here free-left slip roads from Sarjapura Road (towards C) onto Hosur Road towards B, which the sketch stops a few metres short of; a zone touching less than 15 m of a road changes nothing on that road (drawing tolerance).

proposal_151126_actuated.label: Proposal, crossings favour traffic
proposal_151126_actuated._note: Same network as proposal_151126. The new crossings keep traffic green while vehicles keep coming (gaps of 3 s or less), up to 90 s, then give people 18 s. Stands in for a push-button crossing, which with this many people would be pressed every cycle.

proposal_151126_nocross.label: Proposal without the new crossings
proposal_151126_nocross._note: proposal_151126 with the two mid-block crossings left out: slip roads, bus bay and stops, footpaths only.

SE>HS._note: all of this flow is sent through C onto Hosur Road towards B, instead of via A and 100 Feet Road

baseline_whatif._note: WHAT-IF, not data: today's network, with the 250 veh/h assumed from Sarjapura Road (east of A) to Hosur Road (south of B) all routed through C. Paired with proposal_151126_whatif to show what the slip roads could do if that turn is busy.

proposal_151126_whatif.label: Proposal, what-if traffic

SE>HS._note: all of this flow is sent through C onto Hosur Road towards B, instead of via A and 100 Feet Road

proposal_151126_whatif._note: WHAT-IF, not data: proposal_151126 with the same traffic change as baseline_whatif.

vehicles._tag: ASSUMED model behaviour: each driver chooses a route when setting off, from travel times seen on the network in the last few minutes (SUMO rerouting device, at departure only). Without it every vehicle takes the shortest empty-road route, so a new link or a new queue changes nothing. Rerouting on the way (every 2 minutes) was tried but crashes SUMO 1.28 on this network in about half the runs. Buses keep their timetabled routes.
